clue.text: One modifying poor sight, not good, with start and finish of treatment?

definitions.text: One modifying poor sight, not good, with start and finish of treatment?

indicators.note: modifying means altering, so the pooled letters are rearranged
'not good' means the good letter is left out of the fodder
the start and finish of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: its first and last letters are both T

explanation.surface: A description of a clinician who corrects defective eyesight from the first to the last of a course of treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: POOR SIGHT loses its G ('not good'), and the T at each end of 'treatment' joins in; 'modifying' rearranges the ten letters. Read whole, the clue also describes the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An orthoptist is a specialist who diagnoses and treats squints and other faults of eye movement, so modifying poor sight is the job.

clue.text: Strand, the same after its centre is out of reach

definitions.note: Scots sense: a gutter or channel

indicators.note: the phrase for sameness is placed following the trimmed word
removing the middle of the following word leaves only its outside letters

parts.note: the word with its middle three letters taken away
as in 'one and the same'

explanation.surface: Someone stranded on a beach finds the same thing still beyond reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strand' looks like a beach or a thread; here it is the Scots word for a gutter, and RHONE (also rone) is a Scots roof gutter or drainpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots usage both words denote a channel carrying rainwater, such as a roof gutter or drainpipe.

clue.text: Giant bivalve shrivelled in acid tarn

indicators.note: something shrivelled is twisted out of its shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A huge clam has dried up and withered in a sour mountain pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Tridacna is the genus of giant clams, the largest bivalve molluscs living today in tropical reefs.

clue.text: Large fish, not useful, stored in hold

indicators.note: something stored is kept inside something else, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ho is an old call meaning stop or halt
U/S is short for unserviceable

explanation.surface: A big fish nobody can use is left in a ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' suggests a ship's cargo space, but here it is the old interjection meaning stop, and 'not useful' is the military shorthand for unserviceable.
explanation.definitionFit: The huso is the great sturgeon, or beluga, a very large fish of the Caspian and Black Sea.

clue.text: Crash resounded after parking

indicators.note: the word for sounded is placed following the abbreviation

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a bell resounded, or rang

explanation.surface: A loud crash echoed out just after someone parked.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is British slang for a minor collision of a car or aircraft, so it serves as a synonym.

clue.text: German/Italian deploying some French in supermarket

indicators.note: the French word is placed inside the store name

parts.note: Tesco is Britain's largest supermarket chain
de is French for some, as in du/de la

explanation.surface: A German or Italian shopper trots out a bit of French at the supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash reads as 'German or Italian', a nationality pair; really it means the Italian word for German.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedesco is the Italian adjective and noun meaning German, so it is German rendered in Italian.

clue.text: Isn't muddled about cine abroad, ignorant no longer

definitions.note: 'no longer' marks the word as obsolete

indicators.note: one jumbled group goes around the other
something muddled is jumbled, so the contraction's letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the film word is scrambled too

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confused about foreign films is no longer in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone ceasing to be ignorant; in fact 'no longer' tells you the word meaning ignorant is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Inscient is an obsolete adjective meaning lacking knowledge, the opposite of sciens, knowing, from Latin.

clue.text: Sea fish, salty when not left inside

indicators.note: 'not' says the following abbreviation must be taken away
the letters to remove sit within the word, not at its ends

parts.note: savoury food is salty rather than sweet
VO is verso, the left-hand page of a book

explanation.surface: A fish from the ocean tastes of salt unless it is left in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is not L here but VO, verso, the left-hand page; take it out of SAVOURY to leave SAURY.
explanation.definitionFit: The saury is a slender, long-beaked marine fish of the Atlantic and Pacific, also called the skipper.

clue.text: Stage in dividing cells, calamity when section's removed

indicators.note: something removed is taken away, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: a synonym
S is an abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: A biology note: a cell-division phase goes wrong when part is cut out.
explanation.definitionFit: In mitosis the diaster is the phase when the chromosomes form two star-shaped groups at opposite poles.

clue.text: E.g. cat toyed with bit of breakfast, sort of interloper

indicators.note: a cat that toyed with something batted it about, so these letters are shuffled around

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
a rasher is a slice of bacon

explanation.surface: A cat plays with a scrap of someone's breakfast like an uninvited guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toyed with' seems to join the cat to the breakfast; only 'toyed' works on E.G. CAT, and 'with' adds RASHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatecrasher turns up at a party or event uninvited, which makes them one particular kind of intruder.

clue.text: Part of flower below earth to penetrate mineral

indicators.note: in a down entry, below means the flower part follows the earth letter

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring
the female organ of a flower
to bite is to penetrate, as teeth or acid do

explanation.surface: A flower part buried under soil pushes down into rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistilbite is a zeolite, a hydrated aluminosilicate found as crystals in cavities of volcanic rock.

clue.text: Rain tumbled inside piece of ground for chickweed relative

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits within the word for a patch of land

parts.note: an area is a piece of ground

indicators.note: anything tumbled has been tossed about, so the weather word is reordered

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Rain has fallen on a patch of ground where a chickweed cousin grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Arenaria is the sandwort genus, belonging to the pink family alongside chickweed, so it is a close botanical cousin.

clue.text: Small change in Bangladesh I spotted entering expensive area

indicators.note: the letter goes into the word for expensive

parts.note: posh means smart and costly
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A traveller notices a few coins going into a pricey district of Bangladesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small change' reads as a minor alteration; it is a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The poisha is a monetary unit of Bangladesh, one hundredth of a taka, so it is small coinage there.

clue.text: Coarse cotton universal in sailors making comeback

indicators.note: coming back means running the word the other way
the single letter goes inside the word for seamen

parts.note: tar is a familiar word for a sailor
U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Rough cotton cloth is worn universally by sailors who are returning.
explanation.definitionFit: Surat is a coarse uncoloured cotton cloth, named after the Indian port city from which it was exported.

clue.text: What's in indigo icon? Little new in that

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the word just given

parts.note: an icon is an idol, something revered
N is the short form of new

explanation.surface: A question about what an indigo-coloured icon contains, answered by its small novelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Indol is a crystalline compound obtained from indigo, where it forms the core of the dye molecule.

clue.text: Pink after kiss mostly? Show interruption of blood supply?

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to necrose is to show the tissue death that follows loss of blood supply

indicators.note: the colour comes after the shortened kiss
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
rose is a pink colour

explanation.surface: Someone flushed pink after a long kiss asks whether that shows a problem with blood flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' looks like a blush, but it is the colour ROSE; 'kiss' is the verb NECK, cut short by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To necrose is to undergo necrosis, the death of tissue that commonly results when its blood supply is cut off.

clue.text: What fisherman casts? His medium number

parts.note: the element a fisherman works in
N is an algebraic symbol for a number

explanation.surface: A question and answer about an angler: what he throws out and where.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' refers back to the fisherman, whose working medium is SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean is a variant spelling of seine, a large vertical fishing net that is cast or drawn round shoals.

clue.text: A bird gripped by sickness of parent

indicators.note: something gripped is held inside, so the bird goes within the sickness word

parts.note: mal is French for illness, used in English in such words as mal de mer
taken as written
a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird is in the grip of an illness passed down from a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Maternal means relating to a mother, so it describes things belonging to that kind of parent.

clue.text: Floor grabbing attraction in government as of old

indicators.note: something grabbing holds another thing inside its grasp

parts.note: a stage is a floor or storey of a building
ear in the sense of attention, as in having someone's ear

explanation.surface: Speakers on a floor of parliament fight for attention within government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As of old' tells you the spelling is an obsolete one, a form of steerage in its sense of guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: Stearage is an archaic spelling of steerage, which once meant steering or direction, hence governing or management.

clue.text: Simple game in US? Lacking tact for Central American

indicators.note: lacking something means it is missing, so those letters are removed

parts.note: tic-tac-to is a US spelling of noughts and crosses
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American who can't play noughts and crosses tactfully is from Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: Noughts and crosses is the British name for the grid game Americans call tic-tac-toe, also spelt tic-tac-to; remove TACT from its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tico is an informal name for a Costa Rican, a native of a Central American country.

clue.text: Lizard weapon cut short in India, wild

indicators.note: the trimmed weapon is put inside the country name
running wild means out of order, so the combined letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cutting short removes the end letter of the weapon

parts.note: a firearm, here missing its last letter

explanation.surface: In India a lizard runs wild while a weapon fails to reach it.
explanation.walkthrough: GU goes into INDIA and the whole is rearranged; the country is fodder, not the definition's setting.
explanation.definitionFit: An iguanid is any lizard of the iguana family, which includes the iguanas, anoles and basilisks.

clue.text: Trained pacer, etc — one that's sure to run

indicators.note: a trained animal has been worked into a new shape, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A trained pacer and similar horses will certainly be starting the race.
explanation.walkthrough: In horse racing an acceptor is a horse whose owner has confirmed it will run.
explanation.definitionFit: A racehorse confirmed as a starter after the final declaration stage is called an accepter, so it will definitely race.

clue.text: Irish stored in packing case, cloudy after a fashion

indicators.note: something stored is kept within the box word

parts.note: a crate is a wooden packing case
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Irish goods packed in a crate turn out murky in a way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cirrate means bearing cirri, wispy curls, and cirrus is also the name of a wispy high cloud, so it is loosely cloudy.

clue.text: Number one bell I turned? It often requires a key

indicators.note: turned round means the whole string is read from the other end

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
Roman numeral one
the sound a small bell makes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer turns as number one; a question about what needs a key.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string NO I TING I is read backwards. The definition is a cryptic description: a car's ignition is usually worked by a key.
explanation.definitionFit: The starting system of a motor vehicle is usually switched on by turning a key in its lock.

clue.text: An occupant of the pulpit rerunning tape recorder?

indicators.note: running back over means going the other way, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the indefinite article
Rev. is short for Reverend, a clergyman who preaches

explanation.surface: A preacher replays his sermon on a tape recorder.
explanation.definitionFit: VERA, Vision Electronic Recording Apparatus, was an early BBC video tape recording machine of the 1950s.

clue.text: Flowery tree in bed, not mature

indicators.note: 'not' says the word for mature is taken out

parts.note: bed stands for marriage, as in the marriage bed
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A blossoming tree stands in a flower bed that has not yet grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests a flower bed next to 'flowery'; it means marriage here.
explanation.definitionFit: The marri is a Western Australian eucalyptus that bears big showy clusters of cream blossom.

clue.text: Shrubby plant, name for hard old wood

parts.note: hebe is an evergreen shrub from New Zealand
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A gardener names a bush and asks which hard timber it gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Heben is an obsolete word for ebony, the very dense black timber, hence 'old' in the definition.

clue.text: They're dim-witted on account of extremes of fatuousness

parts.note: o/a is the commercial abbreviation for on account

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Some people are stupid simply because of how foolish they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Oafs are clumsy, stupid people, so they can be described as slow-witted or dull of mind.

clue.text: Work hard on American tree family

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first part sits above what follows

parts.note: to fag is to toil, British slang
US stands for American

explanation.surface: Someone slaves away over an American family of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagus is the botanical genus of beeches, so it names a group of related trees; 'family' is used loosely for genus.

clue.text: Quantity of drugs fit to be nicked, not stable, in Parisian rumpus

parts.note: a bag is a measure of drugs sold

indicators.note: 'not' tells you a word is to be removed from what precedes it

parts.note: nicked is British slang for arrested
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Paris drugs raid: a bag of narcotics, an arrest, and chaos in the stables.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagarre is French for a brawl or scuffle, so in Paris a rowdy fight would be called that.

clue.text: Bitter banned for Muslims? Send it back

indicators.note: sending back means returning it in the opposite direction

parts.note: haram means forbidden under Islamic law

explanation.surface: A pint of bitter served to a Muslim drinker is forbidden, so return it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British beer, which fits the surface, but here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Marah is a Hebrew word for bitterness, taken into English from the bitter waters in Exodus.

clue.text: Like some woollies, in parts they came undone

parts.note: a is a dialect pronoun for they, used in some regions
stitches or tights ran when they came undone

explanation.surface: Pieces of knitwear coming apart at the seams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In parts' means in certain districts, flagging the dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aran describes the thick cabled knitwear from the Aran Islands, so it is a type of jumper pattern.

clue.text: Bury ma you'll find thus in the forest swamp

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the woodland word is what ma becomes when put away this way, so taking ma back out recovers the vessel

parts.note: umarn is a swampy pine forest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Laying mother to rest in a forest bog.
explanation.walkthrough: Put MA IN an URN and you get U-MA-RN, the forest swamp; so ma is literally inurned, and INURN means bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To inurn is to put ashes in an urn, and so to entomb or lay to rest.

clue.text: Salad veg displaying strong smell inspired frenzy

parts.note: BO is body odour
a rage is a frenzy

explanation.surface: A pungent salad leaf provokes a fit of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a herb whose young leaves and blue flowers are eaten in salads, so it counts as a salad vegetable.

clue.text: Measures strength of obligations limiting eaterie

indicators.note: to limit is to set bounds around, so one word hems in the other

parts.note: ties are bonds or obligations
trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant

explanation.surface: Someone gauges how binding the contracts are on a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To titrate a solution is to find its concentration by adding a reagent of known strength.

clue.text: Restationed sentinels succeeded in remaining inaudible

indicators.note: restationed means posted afresh in new places, so the guards' letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: Guards moved to new posts manage to keep perfectly quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Silentness is the condition of making no sound, so it equates to keeping hushed throughout.
